about: Held-out corpus C, the second blind set (50 cases), for measuring the Sahoshi person-name and age redactor with a third set of names, places and shapes: 'a man named', 'one X', couples sharing a surname, surname-only references after Mr. and Mrs., joined initials (T.K.), Title Case and ALL-CAPS headlines, names fused with the suffix -babu, Western digits inside Bengali text, Banglish posts with ages written as 'N bochorer', and person-free items around metro stations, roads and pumping stations named after people. It was written blind: the author never opened, read or searched the redaction code or its tests, so the measured recall and damage are honest. Every person in it is invented, built from common Bengali, Hindi/Bihari, Marwari, Muslim, Sikh, Christian and Anglo-Indian Kolkata given names and surnames; none is a public figure and none refers to a real case. Labels: 'names' lists every word of every person name as it appears in the text (Latin words match as whole words; Bengali/Devanagari words are given bare, without case endings such as -er/-ke, and must be substrings; initials are included as written; titles and honorifics such as Mr, Smt, Shri, Dr, SI, Inspector, শ্রী, শ্রীমতী, ডাঃ, ডাক্তার, श्री, डॉ. are not name words). 'ages' lists every age or age/sex marker that must not survive, as the shortest identifying substring (the number, or the shorthand such as 24F, 27/M, F(23), M, 31). 'keep' lists up to three substrings that must survive redaction: Kolkata place names (many of them containing a person's name, such as roads, parks and metro stations) and ordinary content words. Tiers are news_regional, aggregator and social_unverified. The corpus is scored by tests/test_heldout_recall.py.
